name: The Law Nobody Asked For

pick.label: Pick a law
pick.heading: Pick a law and win an election with it
lead: Some parties are founded to fight for big causes: climate, housing, the economy. Others are founded because a few people got very, very annoyed about one small thing.

Start a one-issue party with a law nobody asked for, and persuade the country to vote for it. Here are some ideas, but you can choose your own. *Nothing about real parties or real politicians, please: make up your own.*
pick.hint: Or click one to choose it.
pick.note: Obviously I’m not looking for a serious manifesto. Some of these laws would be quietly popular, and some would start a riot in the Späti queue. Both are welcome.

shelf.head: Getting around
items: Stand on the right, walk on the left, or else

shelf.head: Big ideas
items: A day off on your birthday
Free ice cream when it’s over 30 degrees

rows: Which law are you campaigning for?
Be precise: who has to do what, and from when?
Which voters will queue round the block for this?
Who will be furious, and what will they say about you?
Rallies, TikTok, a celebrity, a catchy song, door-to-door with free cake…
Three to five words that will be on every poster in Berlin.

values.says: Every pavement in Berlin gets a fast lane and a slow lane, like a motorway. Dawdling in the fast lane, or stopping dead at the top of the U-Bahn stairs to look at your phone, costs 15 euros.
values.fans: Anyone who has ever missed a train stuck behind four people walking side by side. So, everyone, including the four people.
values.enemies: Tourists on Unter den Linden, and every couple in love. They’ll call me a heartless monster, and they’ll have a point.
values.campaign: A video of me overtaking slow walkers on Friedrichstraße to dramatic music. It will go viral for the wrong reasons, but that still counts.

yours.label: Your law
yours.heading: Your campaign
yours.lead: Fill it in on your own phone or laptop (it stays on your device), and be ready to tell the class about your law in a few sentences.

rank.label: The election
rank.heading: Which law wins the election?
rank.placeholder: The law, e.g. A fast lane for pedestrians
rank.lead: Each student makes their pitch in a few sentences. Add it, then argue it into place: the landslide winner at the top, the lost deposit at the bottom.
